text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the July 18 editions of Russian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A series of decrees on army reform, signed by President Yeltsin this week, form only a part of a dramatic transformation awaiting the armed forces.
- A former Soviet spy walks free out of a Swedish prison before the end of his term because of poor health.
- Foreign investment in Russia remains low despite certain positive changes in the economy.
- The biggest advertisers in Russia have formed an association in an attempt to drive down prices for commercial advertising.
- A big Soviet-era Russian radar station in Azerbaijan, often subject of a heated debate between the two countries, in real life seems to be of rather poor, if any, value to Moscow.
- Russia has many more natural monopolies than we can imagine, says Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.
- Chairman of Russia's state-owned St Petersburg television channel, earmarked to merge with the second Russian television channel, has offered to resign.
- Russian borderguards at the Sheremetyevo-2 international airport in Moscow have spotted over three thousand passengers with fake or irregular documents this year.

- Moscow continues to turn a deaf ear on calls to make public archive documents, captured by the Soviet army at the end of World War Two, which could shed light on the fate of the ignominious 'Nazi gold'.
- Russian servicemen to be discharged as a result of the planned army reform are likely to go on a last pilfering binge before going home.
- The government approves a system of stricter controls over natural monopolies.
